The limit for the second year will be elevation 2125, for the third year elevation 2200, for the fourth year elevation 2265, and for the fifth year elevation 2315. This procedure will leave as little dam foundation as possible exposed and open to erosion during each year. Once placement of rockfill has begun on the downstream toe (lowest part of the dam) foundation) the fill itself will serve to slow runoff and filter sediment. The top surface of the dam will be sloped to direct runoff upstream away from Howard Creek. Runoff will also be diverted into stabilized areas along the abutments were necessary. Any areas cleared beyond the limits of the completed fill (such as at the abutments for equipment access) will be stabilized as soon as practical using permanent vegetation and diversions. Silt fences, brush barriers, diversions, erosion control fabric or other measures will also be used as necessary during dam construction. At the end of each construction season exposed areas will be stabilized with grading and sowing of temporary or permanent grasses until the beginning of the subsequent construction season.
West Dam - The sediment basin in West Bad Creek will be functioning when construction begins on the West Dam. The basin will trap runoff from dam construction and hold it for plain sedimentation. The dam will be built in one year; therefore, the entire foundation will be cleared and grubbed at one time. Additional clearing beyond the area of fill placement will be limited to that which is necessary for equipment access. These areas will be stabilized using diversions and permanent vegetation as soon as practical.
East Dike - Runoff from the construction of the East Dike will be diverted into the Bad Creek and construction yard sediment basins where it will be held for plain sedimentation. Clearing beyond the area of fill placement will be limited to that which is necessary for equipment access. These areas will be stabilized using diversions and permanent vegetation.
e) Relocation of County Road 171  Approximately one quarter mile of County Road 171 will be relocated as shown on drawing PBK-1014-2. This relocation is in the drainage basin of a tributary of Howard Creek. The new route will pass within 150 feet of the tributary. Grassing, mulching or erosion control fabric will be used on new slopes to stabilize them as soon as practical after completion. Runoff will be collected in ditches and directed to silt fences, brush barriers, or small silt basins to remove sediment before it reaches the stream.
f) Transformer yard  The transformer yard will be located as shown on drawing PBK-1014-2. The proximity of the excavation to several small streams which discharge into Lake Jocassee will require use of a sediment basin. Typical basin dike and outlet are shown on Figure 1.
